Responden Order Sheet 05/11/2024 Heard Mr. Vaibhav P. Shukla, learned counsel for the Digitally ROHIT signed by ROHIT KUMAR petitioners.
Also heard Mr. Malay Jain, learned Panel KUMAR CHANDRA CHANDRA Date:
Lawyer, appearing for the State/respondent Nos.1 and 2024.11.06 10:43:18 +0530 perused the impugned F.I.R. as well as charge-sheet and materials brought on record.

It has been submitted by the learned counsel for the petitioners that the dispute between the petitioner No.1 and respondent No.2 is a matrimonial dispute and the petitioner No.1 has already been granted anticipatory bail by this Court vide order dated 15.07.2024 in MCRCA No. 114 of 2024 and in the said proceeding, the matter was referred to the Mediation Centre of this Court, but mediation between the parties has been failed.
A copy of order granting anticipatory bail to petitioner No.1 has been annexed as Annexure-P/3 at page No.58.

It has been further stated that petitioner No.1 has 60% permanent disability as he has suffered severe head injury which lead to blood clots in brain and he is also suffering from seizure disorder (fits) for which he has gone through surgery and treatment and doctor has advised him to take rest,

sentences.text: as such, he prays for quashment of the entire criminal proceedings initiated against the petitioner No.1 pursuant to the impugned FIR.

Considering the nature and gravity of allegations levelled against petitioner No.1, we do not find any good ground for quashing of the criminal proceeding so far as it relates to petitioner No.1, namely,
Deepak Kumar Sinha, accordingly, the petition filed on behalf of petitioner No.1, namely, Deepak Kumar Sinha is rejected and criminal proceedings against him may go on in accordance with law.

So far as the petitioner Nos. 2 to 4 are concerned, it has been argued by learned counsel for the petitioners that petitioner Nos. 2 to 4 are in laws of respondent No.2 and family members of petitioner No.1 and the proceedings against them is gross abuse of the process of the Court as there are general and omnibus allegations against them.

In support of his contention, he placed reliance upon the judgment passed by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the matter of Geeta Mehrotra and another v. State of Uttar Pradesh and another, reported in (2012) 10 SCC 741.
Issue notice to respondent No.2 on payment of PF as per rules.

entities.text: Geeta Mehrotra and another v. State of Uttar Pradesh and another, reported in (2012) 10 SCC 741
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Notice be made returnable within four weeks.

Taking into consideration the fact that there are general and omnibus allegations against petitioner Nos. 2 to 4, namely Smt. Rewti Sinha, Shashi Kumar Sinha and Usha Sinha, further criminal proceedings in Criminal Case No. 10394/2024 pending before the Court of learned Judicial Magistrate First Class, Raipur pursuant to the FIR bearing Crime No. 07/2024 registered against the petitioners at Police Station - Mahila Thana, Raipur on 09.01.2024 under Sections 498A and 34 of IPC against petitioner Nos. 2 to 4, namely Smt. Rewti Sinha, Shashi Kumar Sinha and Usha Sinha shall remain stayed till the next date of hearing.

Sd/- Sd/-
 (Bibhu Datta Guru) (Ramesh Sinha)
